questions.q: What does the Account Analysis Report show that a trial balance does not?
options: The budget for the next fiscal year
Every journal line that touched one specific account during a period
The chart of accounts structure
The approval hierarchy for an entire company
questions.explain: The Account Analysis Report lists every journal line posted to a specific account, which is the detail a trial balance total doesn't show on its own.

questions.q: Why would an auditor check a sequence-based report on document numbers for manual journals?
options: To calculate currency exchange rates
To approve budget transfers
To confirm completeness — that no document number in the sequence is missing
To reconcile bank statements
questions.explain: Sequence-based review confirms no manual journal document number is missing, a common completeness check in audits.

questions.q: What does an audit trail capture that a journal report does not?
options: The debit and credit amounts of each line
The chart of accounts segment values used
The ledger's functional currency
Who created, edited, approved, and posted a journal, and when
questions.explain: The audit trail is about the process — who did what and when — separate from the financial content a journal report shows.

questions.q: Why do journal reports and audit trails matter together, rather than either alone?
options: Because one proves the accounting ties out and the other proves the process that produced it was followed — both are typically required for a control to hold up
Because journal reports are only used for budgeting
Because audit trails replace the need for journal reports entirely
Because they both show only summarized balances, never detail
questions.explain: Numbers that tie out and a documented trail of who was responsible together satisfy both correctness and control requirements.

questions.q: In the LTV Manufacturing Corporation example, why would a reviewer pull the Account Analysis Report for Utilities Expense?
options: To close the accounting period immediately
To change the account's chart of accounts segment values
To reverse all journals posted to that account
To see every journal line behind the $4,180 balance and judge whether each one is legitimate
questions.explain: The Account Analysis Report is exactly the tool for explaining an account balance by reviewing the journal lines that built it.
